question: What kind of radiation is absorbed by the ozone layer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ultraviolet radiation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ozone layer (in the stratosphere) absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet (UV) radiation. (ओज़ोन परत — पराबैंगनी विकिरण)

 

• Ozone (O₃) molecules absorb UV-B and UV-C wavelengths, preventing most of this harmful radiation from reaching Earth's surface.

 

• The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere, roughly 15-35 km above the Earth's surface.

 

• UV radiation can cause skin cancer, cataracts, and DNA damage; the ozone layer shields life on Earth from these effects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ozone layer depletion is caused mainly by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), and is addressed globally by the Montreal Protocol (1987).

 

• The ozone hole is most pronounced over Antarctica, forming each spring.

 

NOTE

 

• Green radiation (Option 1): Part of the visible spectrum, it largely passes through the atmosphere rather than being absorbed by ozone.

 

• Infrared radiation (Option 2): Mostly absorbed by greenhouse gases like CO₂ and water vapour, not primarily by the ozone layer.

 

• Visible radiation (Option 3): Passes largely unabsorbed through the ozone layer, which is how sunlight reaches and illuminates the Earth's surface.

question: Which of the following organisations, divided into two branches, was established by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Home Rule League.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Home Rule League movement, launched in 1916, had two branches — one led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and another by Annie Besant. (होम रूल लीग — तिलक और एनी बेसेंट)

 

• Tilak founded his Indian Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum, with headquarters at Poona, covering Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar.

 

• Annie Besant founded her Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras, covering the rest of British India.

 

• The movement's famous slogan, associated with Tilak, was "Home Rule is my birthright and I shall have it."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress, at its Calcutta session in 1917.

 

• The movement aimed at securing self-government (Home Rule) within the British Empire, inspired by the Irish Home Rule movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Association (Option 1): Founded by Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose in 1876 in Calcutta; not established by Tilak and Besant.

 

• Theosophical Society (Option 2): Founded by Madame Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott in 1875 in New York; Annie Besant later led it, but it was not founded by Tilak and Besant together.

 

• East Indian Association (Option 3): Founded by Dadabhai Naoroji in London in 1866; unrelated to Tilak and Besant.

question: In which of the following years did India NOT host the ICC Cricket World Cup Tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1983.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India has co-hosted or hosted the ICC Cricket World Cup in 1987, 1996, 2011 and 2023, but NOT in 1983. (क्रिकेट विश्व कप — 1983 इंग्लैंड में आयोजित)

 

• The 1983 Cricket World Cup was held in England, and was famously won by India under Kapil Dev's captaincy, defeating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

 

• The 1987 World Cup (Reliance Cup) was jointly hosted by India and Pakistan — India's first time hosting the tournament.

 

• The 1996 World Cup (Wills World Cup) was jointly hosted by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and the 2011 World Cup was jointly hosted by India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (won by India).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup was hosted solely by India.

 

• India has won the Cricket World Cup three times: 1983, 2011, and 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• 2011 (Option 1): India co-hosted this edition (with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh), so it does not fit "did NOT host."

 

• 1996 (Option 2): India co-hosted this edition, along with Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

 

• 1987 (Option 4): India co-hosted this edition, along with Pakistan.

question:
Match the following books with their respective authors.

Book: a) Tajul Ma'asir, b) Khazain-ul Futuh, c) Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi, d) Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi

Author: i) Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi, ii) Hasan Nizami, iii) Ziauddin Barani, iv) Amir Khusrav
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii; b-iv; c-iii; d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matches are: Tajul Ma'asir by Hasan Nizami; Khazain-ul Futuh by Amir Khusrav; Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi by Ziauddin Barani; Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi. (मध्यकालीन इतिहास ग्रंथ — लेखक मिलान)

 

• Tajul Ma'asir ("Crown of Exploits"), by Hasan Nizami, is one of the earliest Persian histories of Muslim rule in India, covering the reign of Qutbuddin Aibak.

 

• Khazain-ul Futuh ("Treasures of Victory"), by Amir Khusrav, describes the campaigns and conquests of Alauddin Khalji.

 

• Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi, by Ziauddin Barani, chronicles the reigns of the Delhi Sultans up to Firuz Shah Tughlaq; Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi, by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi, covers the Delhi Sultanate up to the reign of the Sayyid ruler Mubarak Shah.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amir Khusrav, called the "Tuti-e-Hind" (Parrot of India), was a celebrated poet, musician and scholar in the courts of several Delhi Sultans.

 

• A separate work also titled Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi was written by Shams Siraj Afif, distinct from Barani's chronicle of the same name.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (a-iii; b-i; c-iv; d-ii): Mismatches all four pairings against the verified attributions above.

 

• Option 3 (a-iv; b-iii; c-i; d-ii): Incorrectly assigns Amir Khusrav to Tajul Ma'asir and Ziauddin Barani to Khazain-ul Futuh.

 

• Option 4 (a-i; b-iii; c-ii; d-iv): Incorrectly assigns Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi to Tajul Ma'asir and Hasan Nizami to Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi.

question: Which of the following options is mostly caused by overpopulation?
option_1: Land and other renewable resources are under pressure
option_3: Reduction in the scarcity of water
option_4: Increase in the area covered by forests
solution_text:
The correct answer is Land and other renewable resources are under pressure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Overpopulation places excessive demand on finite resources, causing land and other renewable resources to come under severe pressure. (जनसंख्या वृद्धि — संसाधनों पर दबाव)

 

• It leads to over-exploitation of land for agriculture, deforestation, and depletion of resources like soil, water and forests faster than they can naturally regenerate.

 

• This results in reduced per-capita availability of resources, environmental degradation, and food and water scarcity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Overpopulation is also linked to unemployment, poverty, and strain on urban infrastructure and public services.

 

• India's population policies, such as the National Population Policy, 2000, aim to stabilise population growth to ease this pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Adequate natural resource storage (Option 2): The opposite is true — overpopulation causes resource depletion, not adequate storage.

 

• Reduction in the scarcity of water (Option 3): Overpopulation increases water scarcity rather than reducing it.

 

• Increase in the area covered by forests (Option 4): Overpopulation typically causes deforestation and shrinking forest cover, not an increase.

question: Which of the following types of direct tax collection increased as of 10 February 2023 budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Personal income tax.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Union Budget 2023-24 estimates, personal income tax collections rose sharply, and for the first time were budgeted to overtake corporate tax collections as the largest component of direct tax revenue. (प्रत्यक्ष कर — व्यक्तिगत आयकर में वृद्धि)

 

• This marked a shift from earlier years, when corporate tax had consistently been the larger share of India's direct tax collection.

 

• The rise reflects a widening income-tax base, improved compliance, and growing formalisation of the economy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Direct taxes (income tax, corporate tax) are levied directly on income or profit, unlike indirect taxes (GST, customs duty), which are levied on goods and services.

 

• The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) administers direct tax collection and policy in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Octroi duties (Option 2): A local/municipal tax on goods entering a town, largely subsumed under GST since 2017; not classified as a rising direct tax in this budget context.

 

• Corporate tax (Option 3): Grew more slowly in this period and was overtaken by personal income tax as the larger source of direct tax revenue.

 

• Commercial tax (Option 4): A state-level indirect (sales) tax, also largely subsumed under GST, not the direct tax that increased in this context.

question: Palladium on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO4) is also known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is the Rosenmund catalyst.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Palladium deposited on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO₄) is known as the Rosenmund catalyst. (रोसेनमुंड उत्प्रेरक — पैलेडियम/बेरियम सल्फेट)

 

• It is used in the Rosenmund reduction, a reaction that selectively reduces acyl chlorides (acid chlorides) to aldehydes without over-reducing them to alcohols.

 

• The barium sulphate support, along with a catalyst poison such as sulphur or quinoline, partially deactivates ("poisons") the palladium, preventing further reduction of the aldehyde product.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rosenmund reduction is named after the German chemist Karl Wilhelm Rosenmund.

 

• It is an important method in organic synthesis for selectively preparing aldehydes from acid chlorides.

 

NOTE

 

• Hillman reaction catalyst (Option 1): Not a standard named catalyst; likely a distractor (possibly confused with the Baylis-Hillman reaction, which uses tertiary amine catalysts like DABCO, not Pd/BaSO₄).

 

• Cannizzaro reaction catalyst (Option 2): The Cannizzaro reaction is a base-mediated disproportionation of aldehydes (using NaOH/KOH), requiring no palladium catalyst.

 

• Aldol reaction catalyst (Option 4): Aldol condensation is catalysed by acids or bases (e.g., dilute NaOH), not by Pd/BaSO₄.

question: Ebony and Mahogany trees are found in which type of forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical evergreen forests.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ebony and Mahogany are hardwood species characteristic of tropical evergreen (rainforest) vegetation. (सदाबहार वन — आबनूस और महोगनी)

 

• Tropical evergreen forests occur in regions with heavy rainfall (over 200 cm annually) and remain green throughout the year, as trees shed their leaves at different times.

 

• Other typical trees of this forest type include rosewood, rubber, and cinchona; in India, these forests are found in the Western Ghats, north-eastern states, and the Andaman-Nicobar Islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests, by contrast, shed leaves for about 6-8 weeks in the dry season and are dominated by species like teak and sal.

 

• Mangrove forests grow in coastal saline/brackish areas (e.g., the Sundarbans) and are dominated by salt-tolerant species like Sundari, not ebony/mahogany.

 

NOTE

 

• Mangrove forests (Option 1): Dominated by salt-tolerant species like Sundari and Rhizophora, not ebony/mahogany.

 

• Tropical deciduous forests (Option 2): Dominated by teak, sal, and sandalwood, and shed leaves seasonally — not ebony/mahogany forests.

 

• Montane forests (Option 4): Found at higher altitudes, dominated by conifers like pine, deodar and fir, not ebony/mahogany.

question: Which party formed the government in Britain in the year 1945?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Labour Party.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Labour Party, led by Clement Attlee, won the 1945 UK general election in a landslide, defeating Winston Churchill's Conservative Party. (लेबर पार्टी — 1945 ब्रिटेन चुनाव)

 

• This victory came shortly after the end of World War II in Europe, and Attlee became Prime Minister, replacing the wartime leader Churchill.

 

• The Attlee government implemented major welfare-state reforms, including the creation of the National Health Service (NHS) in 1948.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Winston Churchill, despite leading Britain through WWII, lost this election due to the public's desire for post-war social and economic reconstruction.

 

• The Labour Party's 1945 manifesto was based on the Beveridge Report (1942), which laid the foundation for the modern British welfare state.

 

NOTE

 

• Democratic Party (Option 1): A major U.S. political party, not a British one.

 

• Socialist Party (Option 3): No major "Socialist Party" formed the 1945 British government; the (democratic-socialist) Labour Party won instead.

 

• Liberal Party (Option 4): Had declined sharply in British politics by 1945 and did not form the government.

question: When was the Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) announced by India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) was announced in 2008. (शुल्क-मुक्त शुल्क अधिमान्यता योजना — 2008)

 

• It was announced by then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on 8 April 2008 at the India-Africa Forum Summit in New Delhi, and formally came into effect on 13 August 2008.

 

• Under the scheme, India offers preferential/duty-free market access to LDCs across a large number of tariff lines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme was notified to the WTO on 5 September 2011.

 

• It covers products constituting roughly 92-98% of India's total tariff lines, benefiting LDC exporters across Asia and Africa.

 

NOTE

 

• 2010 (Option 1): Does not correspond to the year the scheme was announced.

 

• 2009 (Option 2): Incorrect; the announcement predates 2009.

 

• 2006 (Option 3): Incorrect; too early — the scheme was announced two years later, in 2008.

question: Which Ghazal singer was conferred with the prestigious Deenanath Mangeshkar Award in April 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pankaj Udhas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghazal singer Pankaj Udhas was conferred the Master Deenanath Mangeshkar Award at a ceremony held in April 2023. (दीनानाथ मंगेशकर पुरस्कार — पंकज उधास)

 

• The award, instituted in memory of Pandit Deenanath Mangeshkar (father of Lata Mangeshkar), is given annually to eminent personalities for their contributions to Indian arts and society.

 

• The same ceremony that year also honoured other personalities, including Asha Bhosle (with the top Lata Deenanath Mangeshkar Puraskar) and Vidya Balan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pankaj Udhas is celebrated for popularising the ghazal genre in India, through albums such as *Aahat* and songs like *"Chitthi Aayi Hai."*

 

• The Mangeshkar family (Lata, Asha, Hridaynath, Usha, Meena) is one of the most influential musical families in Indian cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Talat Aziz (Option 1): A noted ghazal singer, but not the recipient of this specific award in April 2023.

 

• Ghazal Srinivas (Option 2): A Telugu ghazal singer, not the recipient of this award in April 2023.

 

• Bhupinder Singh (Option 4): A renowned ghazal and playback singer, but not the answer to this specific award/date.

question: In which year was the PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) was launched on 25 October 2021 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. (आयुष्मान भारत स्वास्थ्य अवसंरचना मिशन — 2021)

 

• It is one of the largest pan-India schemes for strengthening healthcare infrastructure, with an outlay of about ₹64,180 crore.

 

• The mission aims to develop the capacities of primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare systems, and to strengthen existing national institutions for detecting and treating new and emerging diseases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-ABHIM was earlier known as the "Pradhan Mantri Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana" before being renamed.

 

• It complements other components of Ayushman Bharat, such as Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY (health insurance) and Health & Wellness Centres.

 

NOTE

 

• 2020 (Option 1): Incorrect year; the mission was launched a year later, in 2021.

 

• 2022 (Option 2): Incorrect; the launch predates 2022.

 

• 2023 (Option 4): Incorrect; the launch predates 2023.

question: Which of the following categories does Gonyaulax belong to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dinoflagellates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gonyaulax is a genus of dinoflagellates, a group of mostly unicellular, flagellated, photosynthetic protists found in marine and freshwater habitats. (गोन्यूलैक्स — डाइनोफ्लैजलेट्स)

 

• Dinoflagellates have two flagella (one longitudinal, one transverse) and a cell wall (theca) made of cellulose plates; many species are bioluminescent.

 

• Gonyaulax is notably associated with "red tides" — harmful algal blooms that release toxins and can cause shellfish poisoning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dinoflagellates are classified under Kingdom Protista, alongside groups like Chrysophytes (diatoms) and Euglenoids.

 

• Some dinoflagellate blooms cause the phenomenon of "sea sparkle," a bioluminescent glow seen in ocean water at night.

 

NOTE

 

• Euglenoids (Option 1): Mostly freshwater flagellates like Euglena, with a protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall — a group distinct from dinoflagellates.

 

• Chrysophytes (Option 2): Includes diatoms and golden algae, a group distinct from dinoflagellates.

 

• Protozoans (Option 3): A broad, non-photosynthetic group of heterotrophic protists (e.g., Amoeba, Paramecium); since Gonyaulax is photosynthetic, it is classified separately as a dinoflagellate.

question: Valabhi, a city of ancient India was the capital of the _________ dynasty from the 5th to 8th Century CE.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maitraka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Valabhi (in present-day Gujarat) was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty, which ruled from the 5th to the 8th century CE. (वलभी — मैत्रक वंश)

 

• The Maitrakas were originally feudatories of the Gupta Empire and became independent after the decline of Gupta power, with Bhatarka as the founder of the dynasty.

 

• Valabhi flourished as a great centre of learning, home to the famous Valabhi University, which rivalled Nalanda as a seat of Buddhist education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited Valabhi during his travels and recorded its prosperity.

 

• Valabhi eventually declined due to repeated Arab invasions in the 8th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Chalukya (Option 2): The Chalukyas ruled from capitals like Vatapi (Badami) and Kalyani in the Deccan region, not Valabhi.

 

• Pallava (Option 3): The Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu, unrelated to Valabhi.

 

• Vakataka (Option 4): The Vakatakas ruled the Deccan with capitals such as Nandivardhana and Pravarapura, not Valabhi.

question: Bharatanatyam dance style is associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of Tamil Nadu. (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

 

• It was traditionally performed by devadasis in Hindu temples, particularly associated with the Thanjavur region, and was later codified by the "Tanjore Quartet."

 

• The dance form draws its theoretical basis from Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra, and combines nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance) and natya (drama).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major classical dance forms of India and their associated states include Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognises Bharatanatyam as one of India's eight classical dance forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Karnataka's associated classical dance form is Yakshagana (a dance-drama), not Bharatanatyam.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Bihar is not traditionally associated with a classical dance form like Bharatanatyam.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): Manipur is associated with the classical dance form Manipuri, distinct from Bharatanatyam.

question: Which type of radiation has very short (<10–³ nm) wavelengths, produced by nuclear explosions, lightning and less dramatic activity of radioactive decay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gamma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation with the shortest wavelengths (typically less than 10⁻³ nm) and the highest frequency and energy in the electromagnetic spectrum. (गामा किरणें — सबसे छोटी तरंगदैर्ध्य)

 

• They are produced by nuclear explosions, lightning, and the radioactive decay of atomic nuclei — particularly during alpha or beta decay, when the resulting nucleus sheds excess energy as gamma photons.

 

• Due to their extremely high energy, gamma rays are highly penetrating and hazardous to living tissue, requiring dense shielding (like lead or thick concrete) to block them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gamma rays are used in medicine for cancer treatment (radiotherapy) and sterilisation of medical equipment.

 

• In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength increases in the order: gamma rays < X-rays < ultraviolet < visible light < infrared < microwaves < radio waves.

 

NOTE

 

• Infra-red (Option 2): Has much longer wavelengths (700 nm to 1 mm) and is associated with heat, not typically produced by nuclear explosions/lightning.

 

• Microwave (Option 3): Has still longer wavelengths (1 mm to 1 m), used in radar and microwave ovens — unrelated to the short-wavelength radiation described.

 

• Ultraviolet (Option 4): Has wavelengths between roughly 10 and 400 nm, notably longer than the sub-10⁻³ nm range described in the question.

question: Which of the following pairs do NOT share any borders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhutan and Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhutan, a landlocked Himalayan country, shares its southern and western borders with the Indian states of Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, but NOT with Meghalaya. (भूटान की सीमाएँ — मेघालय से नहीं लगती)

 

• Bhutan is bordered by China (Tibet) to the north, and by India on its eastern, southern and western sides.

 

• Meghalaya lies further south, bordered by Assam and Bangladesh, and does not touch Bhutan's territory at any point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhutan's total international border with India is about 699 km, spanning four Indian states.

 

• The Indian states bordering Bhutan (Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh) are important for cross-border trade and the broader Bhutan-India relationship.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhutan and Arunachal Pradesh (Option 1): They do share a border, so this pair does not fit "do NOT share any borders."

 

• Bhutan and West Bengal (Option 3): They do share a border, near Jaigaon/Phuentsholing.

 

• Bhutan and Assam (Option 4): They do share a border along Bhutan's southern boundary with Assam.

question: On which of the following dates does India celebrate its Constitution Day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26th November.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India celebrates Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) on 26th November every year. (संविधान दिवस — 26 नवंबर)

 

• This date marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly of India formally adopted the Constitution of India (it came into effect later, on 26 January 1950).

 

• The Government of India began officially observing 26 November as Constitution Day from 2015, coinciding with the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, chief architect of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26th January is celebrated as Republic Day, marking the date the Constitution came into force in 1950.

 

• 15th August is India's Independence Day, marking freedom from British rule in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• 26th January (Option 1): This is Republic Day, when the Constitution came into effect — not the day it was adopted.

 

• 15th August (Option 3): This is Independence Day, unrelated to the Constitution's adoption.

 

• 2th October (Option 4): This is Gandhi Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, unrelated to the Constitution.

question: The organisation that Comptroller and Auditor General heads is known as ___________.
option_4: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department (IAAD). (भारत का नियंत्रक-महालेखा परीक्षक — भारतीय लेखापरीक्षा और लेखा विभाग)

 

• The CAG is a constitutional authority under Article 148 of the Constitution of India, responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and state governments.

 

• The IAAD assists the CAG in preparing audit reports, which are submitted to the President/Governor and subsequently placed before Parliament/State Legislature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CAG is often described as the "guardian of the public purse" and is appointed by the President of India for a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

 

• CAG audit reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Civil Accounts Organisation (Option 1): Functions under the Controller General of Accounts, dealing with government accounting — not headed by the CAG.

 

• Controller General of Accounts (Option 2): A separate authority under the Ministry of Finance responsible for government accounting, distinct from the CAG's audit department.

 

• Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (Option 4): The statutory body regulating the chartered accountancy profession in India, unrelated to the CAG.

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct statement(s) from the following:

1. The UDAN scheme has completed five years since its implementation in 2017.

2. It is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Science and Technology.

3. The Airports Authority of India is the implementing agency of this scheme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statements 1 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is incorrect. The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme, launched in 2017, is the flagship regional connectivity scheme of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, not the Ministry of Science and Technology. (उड़ान योजना — नागर विमानन मंत्रालय)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: UDAN was launched in 2017, so by around 2022 it had completed five years since implementation.

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: UDAN is administered by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, not the Ministry of Science and Technology.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is the implementing agency for the UDAN scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• UDAN aims to make air travel affordable and accessible, including to remote and regional areas, through subsidised airfares on regional routes.

 

• The scheme operates through a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) model, under which airlines are compensated for operating on underserved/unserved routes.

 

NOTE

 

• Only statement 3 (Option 1): Incorrectly excludes statement 1, which is also correct.

 

• Only statement 2 (Option 2): Statement 2 is actually the incorrect one, since UDAN belongs to the Ministry of Civil Aviation, not Science and Technology.

 

• Only statements 2 and 3 (Option 3): Incorrectly includes statement 2, which is factually wrong.

question: Which Indian marathon event is considered the largest marathon in Asia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai Marathon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mumbai Marathon (now known as the Tata Mumbai Marathon) is considered the largest marathon event in Asia by number of participants. (मुंबई मैराथन — एशिया की सबसे बड़ी मैराथन)

 

• First held in 2004, it is organised annually and attracts tens of thousands of runners, including elite international athletes and amateur participants, across categories like the full marathon, half marathon, and dream run.

 

• The event is also notable for its philanthropic scale, raising significant funds for various charities each year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indian marathons include the Delhi Half Marathon (Airtel Delhi Half Marathon) and the Kaveri Trail Marathon in Karnataka.

 

• Pinkathon is a women-only marathon series held across various Indian cities, promoting women's fitness and health.

 

NOTE

 

• Kaveri Trail Marathon (Option 1): A relatively smaller, regional marathon held in Karnataka, not the largest in Asia.

 

• Pinkathon (Option 2): A women-centric fitness marathon series, smaller in scale compared to the Mumbai Marathon.

 

• Delhi Half Marathon (Option 3): A major Indian marathon event, but smaller in participant scale than the Mumbai Marathon.

question: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muslim.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shab-e-Barat is a religious observance celebrated by Muslims, falling on the 15th night of the Islamic month of Sha'ban. (शब-ए-बारात — मुस्लिम त्योहार)

 

• The name translates roughly to the "Night of Forgiveness" or "Night of Records," believed to be a night when God determines the destinies of individuals for the coming year.

 

• It is marked by night-long prayers (Ibadat), visiting the graves of ancestors, offering special prayers (Nawafil), and seeking forgiveness for sins.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shab-e-Barat is observed about two weeks before the start of the holy month of Ramadan.

 

• It is also known by various other regional names, such as Nisf Sha'ban or Laylat al-Baraat, across different Muslim communities.

 

NOTE

 

• Buddhist (Option 2): Buddhist festivals include Buddha Purnima and Losar, unrelated to Shab-e-Barat.

 

• Jain (Option 3): Jain festivals include Mahavir Jayanti and Paryushan, unrelated to Shab-e-Barat.

 

• Parsi (Option 4): Parsi festivals include Navroz and Pateti, unrelated to Shab-e-Barat.

question:
Consider the following statements associated with the India Infrastructure Project Development Fund (IIPDF).

1. IIPDF was set up in 2017.

2. The funds for IIPDF are provided by the Central Government'?

3. This scheme is notified under the Department of Economic Affairs.

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only statement 1 is incorrect; statements 2 and 3 are correct. The India Infrastructure Project Development Fund (IIPDF) was actually set up in 2007, not 2017 as claimed in statement 1. (आईआईपीडीएफ योजना — 2007 में स्थापित)

 

• Statement 1 is incorrect: IIPDF was established in 2007 to support the development of high-quality Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects, not in 2017.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The funds for IIPDF are provided by the Central Government as part of the scheme's central sector funding.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: IIPDF is notified and administered under the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• IIPDF provides financial support (up to 75% as interest-free loans) to Sponsoring Authorities to meet PPP project development expenses such as feasibility studies, legal costs, and transaction advisory fees.

 

• The scheme has been extended and re-approved periodically, including a Central Sector Scheme outlay for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 1): Incorrectly marks statements 2 and 3 as wrong, when in fact only statement 1 is incorrect.

 

• Only 1 and 2 (Option 3): Incorrectly includes statement 2, which is factually correct.

 

• Only 3 (Option 4): Incorrectly identifies statement 3 as wrong, when it is actually correct, and misses statement 1's error.

question: Who among the following was one of the Navratnas of Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Miyan Tansen was one of the Navratnas ("nine gems") of Emperor Akbar's court, celebrated as a legendary Hindustani classical musician. (तानसेन — अकबर के नवरत्न)

 

• Tansen was renowned for his mastery over ragas and is credited with composing or popularising several ragas, such as Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar, and Darbari Kanada.

 

• The Navratnas of Akbar also included figures such as Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Birbal, Raja Todar Mal, Raja Man Singh, and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tansen was originally a disciple of Swami Haridas and later served in the court of Raja Ramchandra of Bandhavgarh before joining Akbar's court.

 

• Akbar bestowed upon Tansen the title "Mian" in recognition of his musical genius.

 

NOTE

 

• Purandar Das (Option 1): A renowned Carnatic music composer of the 16th century, regarded as the "father of Carnatic music," unrelated to Akbar's court.

 

• Swami Haridas (Option 2): A revered saint-musician and Tansen's own guru, but not himself a member of Akbar's Navratnas.

 

• Amir Khusro (Option 4): A celebrated poet and musician of the Delhi Sultanate era (13th-14th century), well before Akbar's reign, so he could not have been one of Akbar's Navratnas.

question: Who has written the book ‘Fearless Governance’, published in January 2021, describing her stint as Governor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiran Bedi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fearless Governance," published in January 2021, was written by Kiran Bedi, describing her experiences and stint as Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry. (निडर शासन — किरण बेदी)

 

• Kiran Bedi, India's first woman IPS officer, served as the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry from 2016 to 2021.

 

• The book reflects on her governance style, administrative reforms, and the challenges faced while holding the constitutional post.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kiran Bedi has authored several other books, including "It's Always Possible," drawing on her long career in law enforcement and public administration.

 

• She was awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1994 for her contributions to public service.

 

NOTE

 

• Draupadi Murmu (Option 1): Served as Governor of Jharkhand before becoming the President of India, but did not write this particular book.

 

• Baby Rani Maurya (Option 2): Served as Governor of Uttarakhand, but is not the author of "Fearless Governance."

 

• Anandiben Patel (Option 4): Served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, but is not the author of this book.
